NAND Manufacturing is moving from Tungsten to Molybdenum (Mo): 3D NAND stopped shrinking sideways a decade ago, it scales by stacking layers. But above ~300 layers, the tungsten word lines wiring every memory cell hit a wall: resistance is too high, fluorine-based chemistry causes leakage, and gap-fill fails in ultra-deep holes.
